doc_name: Nebula Award for Best Game Writing
text: The Nebula Award for Best Game Writing is one of the Nebula Awards, presented annually by the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association (SFWA) for science fiction or fantasy game writing. The Nebula Awards are regarded as one of "the most important of the American science fiction awards" and are described as the "science-fiction and fantasy equivalent" of the Emmy Awards. The Game Writing category is the newest addition to the Nebulas, which began in 1966 with awards for printed fiction only. The Nebula Award for Best Game Writing has been awarded annually since 2019. The push to establish this category was championed by then SFWA president Cat Rambo following the eligibility of game writers for SFWA membership in 2016. According to an SFWA statement from 2018, the category was introduced to reflect how technological advancements have expanded the media used in science fiction and fantasy storytelling. To be eligible, a work must be published in English in the United States, or in English elsewhere in the world if released on a website or in an electronic edition. A game is defined as "an interactive or playable story-driven work which conveys narrative, character, or story background," with no set word count required, but at least one credited writer is necessary. Nominees and winners are selected by SFWA members, though game writers do not need to be members. Works are nominated between December 15 and January 31 each year, with the six receiving the most nominations forming the final ballot—additional nominees may be included in case of ties. Members then vote on the ballot over a one-month period, and the results are announced at the Nebula Awards ceremony in May. Writers are not allowed to nominate their own works, and if a tie occurs in the final vote, it is broken by the number of nominations the work received. Over seven nomination years, 41 games by 121 writers have been nominated, primarily video games, but also including eight books for role-playing game systems and one interactive film. The first award was won by Charlie Brooker for the interactive film Black Mirror: Bandersnatch; the second by a team of nine writers led by Leonard Boyarsky for The Outer Worlds; the third by Greg Kasavin for Hades; the fourth by a team of six writers for Thirsty Sword Lesbians; the fifth by Hidetaka Miyazaki and George R. R. Martin for Elden Ring; the sixth by a team of 16 writers led by Adam Smith for Baldur's Gate 3; and the seventh by a team of writers led by Stewart C. Baker for the interactive fiction game A Death In Hyperspace. Eleven writers have been nominated more than once, with Kate Heartfield and Natalia Theodoridou each having three nominations. Interactive fiction developer Choice of Games has had the most games nominated, with nine over six years. SFWA identifies the awards by the year of publication, which is the year prior to the award year. Entries with a yellow background and an asterisk (*) next to the writer's name are winners or joint winners; all other entries are nominees on the shortlist.
